title: Etale-local etale quotient presentations for affine flat locally quasi-finite relations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For $S$-schemes $V,R$, an equivalence relation $j=(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] means that $j$ is injective on sections over every $S$-scheme $T$ and identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. Write $V/R$ for the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of $T\mapsto V(T)/R(T)$. Assume $V$ is affine, and $s,t$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. There exist a finite set $I$, affine $S$-schemes $W_i$ and etale maps $g_i:W_i\to V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with jointly surjective images, such that, writing $R_i=W_i\times_{g_i,V,s}R\times_{t,V,g_i}W_i$, for each $i\in I$ there are $S$-schemes $\overline W_i,\overline R_i$, an equivalence relation $\overline R_i\to\overline W_i\times_S\overline W_i$ with etale projections, and an isomorphism of fppf sheaves $W_i/R_i\simeq\overline W_i/\overline R_i$. All these objects and the finite covering belong to the chosen site bound. The finite set may be empty when $V$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), proof, affine locally quasi-finite case: finite etale quasi-splitting cover, division by the open finite locally free subgroupoid, and the open-identity etaleness argument. proof.text: The given equivalence relation has a canonical groupoid structure [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]: identities, inversion and composition are the unique arrows with the prescribed endpoints; the groupoid laws hold because an arrow is determined by its endpoints. Apply [lem-trf-affine-square-monomorphism-absolute-separated] to $V$ and $j$ to obtain that $R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated, even when $S$ is not separated. Factor this structure morphism through each of $s,t:R\to V$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] gives that $s$ and $t$ are separated. Thus the separated-projection hypotheses for pointed quasi-splitting are available.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), affine locally quasi-finite case; separatedness as in spaces.tex Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-groupoid-pointed-quasisplitting] at every $v\in V$. It supplies affine etale charts $g_v:W_v\to V$ whose images contain $v$, restricted groupoids $R_v$, and open finite locally free subgroupoids $P_v\subset R_v$. The images are open by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], specialized to scheme morphisms (schemes are algebraic spaces). They cover $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], choose a finite subcover and label its charts by a finite set $I$. These are the original charts of the subcover, so their $P_i$ are retained without any shrinking. If $V$ is empty, take $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), paragraph beginning Choose u in U: pointwise Tag 04S0 charts and finite covering

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and abbreviate $W=W_i$, $A=R_i$, $P=P_i$. The fibre-product description shows that $A(T)$ is exactly the relation $g_i(x)\sim g_i(y)$ on $W(T)$, so $A\to W\times_SW$ is monic and $P\to W\times_SW$ is monic. The projections $A\to W$ are flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite by the quasi-splitting input. In particular the first projection is locally of finite type, by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf] to $A\to W\times_SW\to W$ to obtain the separatedness and local quasi-finiteness of the relation map required for division. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-divide-finite-flat-subgroupoid] now hold: $W$ is affine, $P$ is a subgroupoid, its projections are finite locally free, and its relation map is monic. Obtain $q:W\to\overline W$, affine $\overline W$, and a groupoid $(\overline W,\overline R)$ restricting along $q$ to $(W,A)$. Also $q$ is surjective finite locally free, $P=W\times_{\overline W}W$, and $P=A\times_{\overline R,\overline e}\overline W$.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), quasi-split affine case: application of Tag 04S4 (lemma-divide-subgroupoid)

proof.text: By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and [def-pc-fppf-site], the singleton $\{q:W\to\overline W\}$ is an fppf covering. Use the restriction formula from division and put $B=\overline R\times_{\overline s,\overline W}W$. The arrow $A=W\times_{\overline W,\overline t}\overline R\times_{\overline s,\overline W}W\to B$ is a base change of $q$, hence an fppf covering by the site axioms. The composite $A\to B\to W$ is the original flat locally finitely presented projection. The source-and-target clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent], with target cover $W\to\overline W$ and source cover $A\to B$, implies that $\overline s$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Interchanging $s$ and $t$ proves the same assertions for $\overline t$. No source-local assertion for etaleness is used.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), factorization through R-bar x_U-bar U; source and target descent of flatness and local finite presentation

proof.text: The morphism $A\to\overline R$ is the composite of two base changes of the fppf covering $q$; it is therefore an fppf covering by the base-change and composition axioms [def-pc-fppf-site]. The cartesian unit square supplied by [lem-sfb-divide-finite-flat-subgroupoid] identifies its pullback of $\overline e:\overline W\to\overline R$ with the open immersion $P\hookrightarrow A$. Apply the target-local open-immersion assertion of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to conclude that $\overline e$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), cartesian unit square and descent of the open immersion

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-open-unit-etale] to $(\overline W,\overline R)$: step 4 gives flat locally finitely presented projections and step 5 gives an open unit. Thus $\overline s,\overline t$ are etale. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-restriction-quotient] to this groupoid and the fppf covering $q$. Its restriction is $(W,A)$ and its relation map is monic by step 3, so $\overline R\to\overline W\times_S\overline W$ is monic and is an equivalence relation. The same cited statement gives the canonical isomorphism $W/A\simeq\overline W/\overline R$ of fppf sheaves. This constructs all the required data for each $i$.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), Tag 02VH quotient comparison and final open-unit etaleness argument

proof.text: The point-indexed choices and the constructed schemes can be taken in the universes fixed in [def-weil-size-convention]: all constructions use the stated bounded sites, affine etale charts and finite fibre products and quotients from the cited inputs. Passing to representatives in the chosen skeleton preserves the morphisms and their properties. The finite subcover is a set in the same bound, including its empty case. This verifies the size clause as well as the finite covering clause.

lean.statement: theorem fppf_relation_etale_replacement {S : Scheme.{u}} {R V : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [IsAffine V.left] [Flat s.left] [Flat t.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] (hs : s.left.IsLocallyQuasiFinite) (ht : t.left.IsLocallyQuasiFinite) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Finite I) (W : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i : I, W i ⟶ V), (∀ i : I, IsAffine (W i).left ∧ Etale (g i).left) ∧ (∀ v : V.left, ∃ (i : I) (w : (W i).left), (g i).left w = v) ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ (Wbar Rbar : Over S) (sbar tbar : Rbar ⟶ Wbar), Mono (prod.lift sbar tbar) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ Wbar ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ Rbar, r ≫ sbar = a ∧ r ≫ tbar = b)) ∧ Etale sbar.left ∧ Etale tbar.left ∧ Nonempty ((presheafToSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type (u + 1))).obj (coequalizer (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map (restrictedEtaleRelationSource s t (g i))) (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map (restrictedEtaleRelationTarget s t (g i)))) ≅ (presheafToSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type (u + 1))).obj (coequalizer (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map sbar) (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map tbar)))
